transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: James Carter (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Montara - Head of ML), Rajiv Menon (Montara - Infra), Hannah Lee (Montara - Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets for real-time scoring, concurrency requirements, streaming support, and token/sec benchmarking to decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Customer emphasized strict p95 < 150ms for short prompts, 95th at scale under concurrency 200, several security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC).

Topics:
- Current infra and traffic patterns
- p95 targets and SLA expectations
- Token/sec benchmarking approach and sample workloads
- Streaming and stop-token behavior
- KV/prefix caching and batching strategies
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, costs and SLAs

Transcript:
[00:00] James Carter: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm James with Redwood, this is Sofia our solutions engineer, hows it going?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: hi, thanks for organizing. quick note, we only have ~40 minutes, so would love to hit the latency, throughput, and security questions early.
[00:12] Sofia Patel: totally, we planned to run through p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and then Q&A. rajiv, can you start with current infra?
[00:18] Rajiv Menon: yeah sure. so we run inference for fraud-detection scoring, two model sizes roughly 1.3B and 7B, avg seq length 120 tokens, tail up to 800 in some flows. QPS is spiky — baseline 60 qps, peak 220 qps for 30-45s bursts. p95 today on our in-house is around 120-160ms for the small model, larger model p95 ~420ms which is borderline.
[00:44] Hannah Lee: and our customer-facing requirement is p95 under 150ms for the small model for real-time flows, 99 is less important but p95 is key.
[00:52] Sofia Patel: ok that helps. quick clarifying q — when you say p95 150ms, is that end-to-end including network, or just server latency?
[00:59] Lena Ortiz: end-to-end ideally, but at minimum server-side p95 should be <=120ms. network adds ~15-30ms from our regions.
[01:10] James Carter: good — that maps well to Hosted/ Dedicated choices. hosted can hit those numbers for small models with streaming and batching tuned, dedicated gives more predictable throughput for your peak bursts. private is an option if you want VPC and full control but has more ops overhead.
[01:25] Rajiv Menon: one of our concerns is kv cache behavior — we heavily prefix-cache common user history so we need efficient KV reuse and low cold-start for new sessions. how does Redwood handle kv cache across requests and instances?
[01:38] Sofia Patel: great q. our runtime supports persistent KV caching per route and per pod; we also have fast prefix caching that avoids re-attending cached tokens. with dedicated you can pin workloads to a single pool and get higher cache hit rates. hosted uses smart routing to try and keep affinity but for strongest guarantees dedicated or private is recommended.
[01:58] Lena Ortiz: any numbers on how caching impacts p95?
[02:02] Sofia Patel: in our internal tests, with high prefix hit rates (>70%) we see token generation latency drop by ~30-40% for mid-sized contexts. so p95 for small-model cases often moves from 140ms down to sub-100ms. but it depends on sequence length and batch behavior.
[02:20] James Carter: and batching — we do continuous batching with latency SLO controls. you can set max batch waiting time and target throughput. for real-time flows you'd set a low batch window (like 5-10ms) to keep latency predictable.
[02:33] Hannah Lee: about streaming — we need partial outputs to our app as tokens arrive, can you stream and still meet p95?
[02:40] Sofia Patel: yes, streaming is supported. streaming response time is dominated by first-token latency; we optimize that separately. p95 for first-token is what you should watch for streaming UX — after that tokens stream at tokens/sec rates.
[02:53] Rajiv Menon: tokens/sec — how do you benchmark that? we want to understand end-to-end tokens/sec for 120-token sequences vs long 512 contexts.
[03:01] Sofia Patel: we provide a token/sec benchmarking template. typical small-model throughput on a gpus depends on quantization and kernel selection; e.g., a 1.3B quantized to 4-bit on A10/GPU* runs ~150-300 tokens/sec/core in our tests for generation workloads. For 7B on an H100-like instance you might see 400-800 tokens/sec depending on seq length and KV caching. we'll share exact benchmarks and run with your model if you can provide an export or sample weights.
[03:29] Lena Ortiz: hm those numbers are a bit abstract. can we get p95 latencies tied to concurrency? our pattern: 60 qps baseline, 200 concurrent during spikes, and 2-3k daily peak.
[03:40] James Carter: absolutely. typical approach — we run a token/sec benchmark plus a concurrency sweep. we'll simulate your traffic shapes (short vs long sequences) and report p50, p95, p99. For hosted, we can run a pilot on a reserved sandbox and give numbers; for dedicated we can size GPU pools to hit your p95 under the concurrency profile.
[03:56] Rajiv Menon: and networking — if hosted, do you have regional endpoints? we need EU + NA redundancy and data residency for some customers.
[04:05] Sofia Patel: yes regional endpoints and routing policies. for data residency or strict controls, private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is preferred. Hosted keeps data encrypted in transit and at rest, with SOC2 controls, but dedicated/private adds isolation.
[04:18] Hannah Lee: on security, Rajiv asked about KMS and audit logs. do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:23] James Carter: yes we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Dedicated and Private, hosted supports provider-managed keys but we do have bring-your-own-key options depending on contract. Audit logs and token-level tracing are in Redwood Console as an add-on.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: ok good. back to latency targets — can you share a sample run with p95 < 120ms server-side for our 1.3B?
[04:48] Sofia Patel: we can. action: we'll run a hosted baseline with your typical prompt distribution, 120 tokens median, and report p50/p95/p99. Would you be able to provide a representative corpus and a small model snapshot or weights?
[05:00] Lena Ortiz: we can provide a distilled checkpoint and sample prompts, yes. also we care about failure modes — graceful degradation when capacity is constrained. we prefer automatic fallback to a smaller model with preserved latency.
[05:11] James Carter: Redwood supports smart routing — policy-based fallback to cheaper/ smaller variants when capacity is constrained. Rollouts can be canaryed and you can set fallback rules by route.
[05:23] Rajiv Menon: cost question — how different is hosted vs dedicated on unit cost for tokens when you need consistent p95 at high concurrency?
[05:29] James Carter: hosted is optimized for flexibility and low time-to-value; unit cost can be higher under sustained heavy loads. Dedicated gives committed capacity and predictability — per-token cost typically drops with reserved capacity. We'll provide a pricing matrix — depends on model, quantization, and reserved hours.
[05:44] Hannah Lee: about quantization: we saw some quality regressions last time we tried 4-bit on our 7B. do you do quantization-aware tuning?
[05:51] Sofia Patel: yes, we have model-specific quantization profiles and quality monitoring. Redwood Optimize suggests profiles per workload and we can run evals against your prompt set to validate quality before enabling aggressive quantization.
[06:03] Lena Ortiz: perfect. one more technical: concurrency 200 — do you recommend more smaller GPUs or fewer larger ones?
[06:10] Sofia Patel: depends on your model mix. for many small-model, many-small approach (e.g., multiple A10s or M60s) gives better isolation and faster cold-starts; for very large models H100-class with model parallelism is more efficient. We'll profile with your weights to recommend an optimal pool.
[06:27] Rajiv Menon: what about latency SLO enforcement? can we have automated alerts on p95 regressions?
[06:33] James Carter: yes, Redwood Console supports per-route SLOs, alerting, and automatic rollback/ routing changes if thresholds are breached.
[06:41] Hannah Lee: okay, timeline — we'd like to decide in two weeks. can you run an initial hosted pilot and a dedicated sizing proposal?
[06:48] James Carter: yes. Sofia will run a hosted baseline and we will size a dedicated pool and share pricing.
[06:54] Sofia Patel: action notes — i'll need sample prompts, a small checkpoint, and your traffic distribution (qps, burst duration). Also please indicate which flows need streaming vs batch.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: i'll drop that into the shared folder after the call.
[07:10] James Carter: great — any other questions?
[07:12] Rajiv Menon: just one: when you say first-token latency is optimized, what numbers do you typically see for 1.3B on hosted?
[07:18] Sofia Patel: first-token p95 for 1.3B in hosted tests is often in the 60-110ms range depending on quantization and regional network. With prefix cache hits it can be sub-50ms.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: that sounds promising. can you also run a tokens/sec benchmark that reports effective tokens/sec under our concurrency and with streaming enabled?
[07:38] Sofia Patel: yes — we'll include tokens/sec, average token latency, and p95 for first-token and full-response.
[07:45] Hannah Lee: for next steps can we get the benchmarking template now?
[07:48] James Carter: i'll send the template and a sample benchmark script after the call, and include a checklist for the materials we need.
[07:56] Lena Ortiz: thanks. one quick compliance q — do you have an SOC2 report we can share with procurement?
[08:01] James Carter: yes i'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs in the security packet; Rajiv i'll cc you.
[08:07] Rajiv Menon: thanks. also interested in encryption-in-transit details and retention policy for logs and tokens.
[08:12] Sofia Patel: we'll include retention and encryption details in the packet; dedicated/private options offer more control including customer-managed keys.
[08:21] James Carter: ok recap and next steps — Sofia runs hosted baseline and tokens/sec, James sends pricing and security packet, Rajiv supplies traffic distribution and Lena supplies sample prompts and checkpoint. Follow-up demo scheduled for next Wednesday?
[08:35] Hannah Lee: next Wednesday works, we'll confirm via calendar.
[08:40] James Carter: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and action items.
[08:44] Lena Ortiz: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
